literal: Captured his Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, palace attendant of the third rank, Cloud-Banner general, governor of Xu and Yan provinces Liu Xiangru. Juan 98, Biography of Xiao Yan, reads: "Captured his Cloud-Banner general, governor of Xu and Yan provinces Shen Yu; beheaded his Superlative Fierce general, governor of Qi province Liu Xiangru."
idiomatic: They captured his left vice minister of the Secretariat, a palace attendant of the third rank and Cloud-Banner general who was governor of Xu and Yan provinces, Liu Xiangru. Juan 98 (Biography of Xiao Yan) has: they captured Cloud-Banner general and governor of Xu and Yan Shen Yu, and beheaded Superlative Fierce general and governor of Qi Liu Xiangru.

literal: Here below "governor of Xu and Yan provinces" text is missing, causing erroneous conflation into one person.
idiomatic: Text is missing after "governor of Xu and Yan provinces," which wrongly merges two men into one.

literal: Moreover, vice minister and palace attendant of the third rank are very high ranks; one ought not add only the "Cloud-Banner" military title; border prefectural governors also could not hold such offices and titles.
idiomatic: A vice minister and palace attendant of the third rank are exalted posts; they cannot be reduced to the Cloud-Banner military title alone, and a frontier prefect could not bear such a combination of offices.

literal: There must be error.
idiomatic: The passage must be corrupt.

literal: Made palace attendant, grand guardian, chief minister with an open office, Prince of Leping Erzhu Shilong palace attendant of the third mentor rank: in all editions "mentor" is written "rank."
idiomatic: Erzhu Shilong, prince of Leping, already palace attendant, grand guardian, and chief minister with an open office, was made palace attendant of the third mentor rank; every edition writes "mentor" (shi) as "rank" (si).

literal: Comment: Shilong already held "open office"—how could there be adding "palace attendant of the third rank"?
idiomatic: Shilong already held an open office; he could not also receive the ordinary palace attendant of the third rank.

literal: Juan 75, Biography of Erzhu Shilong, states: "The Former Deposed Emperor specially established the office of palace attendant of the third mentor rank, ranking below the three dukes; Shilong was appointed to it.
idiomatic: Juan 75 (Biography of Erzhu Shilong) says the Former Deposed Emperor created a special post of third-rank mentor, below the three dukes, and gave it to Shilong:

literal: " Here "rank" is corruption of "mentor"; now corrected according to the biography.
idiomatic: Here "rank" (si) is a corruption of "mentor" (shi); the biography is followed.

literal: Year 2, spring, third month: the Duke of Qi, Filial and Martial King, defeated Erzhu Tianguang and others at Hanling. Beishi juan 5 writes "third month" as "intercalary second month."
idiomatic: In year 2, spring, third month, the Duke of Qi, Filial and Martial King, defeated Erzhu Tianguang and others at Hanling; Beishi juan 5 has "intercalary second month" instead of "third month."

literal: According to this year
idiomatic: For that year

literal: intercalary third month.
idiomatic: there was an intercalary third month.

literal: The battle of Hanling was in the intercalary third month, repeatedly seen in this juan below in the Former Deposed Emperor annal and in Beishi juan 6, Qi basic annals; here "third month" lost "intercalary" above; Beishi then corrupted "three" to "two."
idiomatic: Hanling fell in the intercalary third month, as repeated below in this juan (Former Deposed Emperor annal) and in Beishi juan 6 (Qi basic annals). Here "intercalary" dropped before "third month"; Beishi further changed "three" to "two."

literal: Pacification-East general Zhang Senkai states: "Above already wrote 'Pacification-East'; here it should not again be Pacification-East; the Former Deposed Emperor annal has 'Campaign-East,' which is correct.
idiomatic: Zhang Senkai notes: "Pacification-East was already written above; this line should not repeat it. The Former Deposed Emperor annal's Campaign-East is correct.

literal: The character 'Pacification' was carried down from above by error."
idiomatic: The word 'Pacification' was copied down from the earlier line by mistake."

literal: Palace attendant, rapid-as-lightning cavalry general, chief minister with an open office, Prince of Qinghe Dan, palace attendant of the third mentor rank: in all editions "mentor" is corrupted to "rank."
idiomatic: Prince of Qinghe Dan, already palace attendant, rapid-as-lightning cavalry general, and chief minister with an open office, was made palace attendant of the third mentor rank; all editions corrupt "mentor" to "rank."

literal: Corrected according to juan 75, Biography of Erzhu Shilong.
idiomatic: Emended from juan 75 (Biography of Erzhu Shilong).

literal: See collation note in this juan
idiomatic: See the collation note in this juan
(note 3)

literal: Xia province migrants Guo Qian held You province in revolt; Governor Yuan Ni abandoned the city and fled. Qian's Examining Differences, juan 28, states: "You is not a province name; Zizhi tongjian juan 155
idiomatic: Guo Qian of the Xia-province migrants seized You province and rebelled; Governor Yuan Ni abandoned the city and fled. Qian's Examining Differences (juan 28) says, "You is not a province name; Zizhi tongjian juan 155

literal: reads Qing province; should follow that.
idiomatic: has Qing province, which should be adopted."

literal: " Comment: This book, juan 16, Biography of Prince of Changshan Zun, appendix Yuan Ni biography, and Beiqishu juan 19, Biography of Cai Jun, show Yuan Ni at this time was governor of Yan province; the unrest occurred in Yan province.
idiomatic: This book juan 16 (Prince of Changshan Zun, appendix on Yuan Ni) and Beiqishu juan 19 (Cai Jun) place Yuan Ni as governor of Yan province when the revolt broke out there.

literal: "You province" is indeed corrupted text; Tongjian's "Qing province" also has no basis; the province Guo Qian held should read "Yan province."
idiomatic: "You province" is plainly wrong, and Tongjian's "Qing province" is equally unsupported; Guo Qian's base should read Yan province.

literal: Made palace attendant, rapid-as-lightning cavalry general Feng Longzhi: in all editions "Long" is written "Yin."
idiomatic: Feng Longzhi was made palace attendant and rapid-as-lightning cavalry general; every edition writes "Long" as "Yin."

literal: Comment: At the time there was no person "Feng Yinzhi"; Qian's Examining Differences, juan 28, states: "'Yinzhi' must be corruption of 'Longzhi.'
idiomatic: No Feng Yinzhi existed then. Qian's Examining Differences (juan 28) says "Yinzhi" is a corruption of "Longzhi."

literal: " Qian's view is correct; now corrected.
idiomatic: Qian is right; the text is emended accordingly.

literal: Made Minister of Works Gao Ganyu commissioner with full powers, rapid-as-lightning cavalry general, chief minister with an open office, palace attendant of the third rank. Zhang Senkai states: "Below 'palace attendant of the third rank' the four characters 'governor of Xu province' were omitted; the text below and the Biography of Gao Gan
idiomatic: Gao Ganyu, minister of works, was made commissioner with full powers, rapid-as-lightning cavalry general, chief minister with an open office, and palace attendant of the third rank. Zhang Senkai says the four words "governor of Xu province" dropped out after "palace attendant of the third rank," as the following passage and the Biography of Gao Gan

literal: (Beiqishu juan 21)
idiomatic: (Beiqishu juan 21)

literal: can verify."
idiomatic: confirm."

literal: Commissioner with full powers, commander-in-chief of military affairs of the He, Wei, and Bu three provinces: Qian's Examining Differences, juan 28, states: "Bu is not a province name; likely corruption of the character 'Shan.'"
idiomatic: As commissioner with full powers commanding the He, Wei, and Bu three provinces: Qian's Examining Differences (juan 28) notes that Bu is not a province name and is probably a corruption of Shan.

literal: Palace attendant, grand master, Duke of Nanyang Bao Ju, grand guardian, chief minister with an open office, palace attendant: Beishi juan 5, part 2, writes "grand master" as "grand guardian."
idiomatic: Bao Ju, duke of Nanyang, palace attendant and grand master, was made grand guardian, chief minister with an open office, and palace attendant; Beishi juan 5, part 2, writes "grand master" as "grand guardian."

literal: Comment: Bao Ju was already grand master—how could there be promoting from grand master to grand master; the character "master" must be wrong.
idiomatic: Bao Ju was already grand master; he could not be promoted from grand master to grand master—the title "master" must be mistaken.

literal: Commissioner with full powers, pacification-north general, commander-in-chief, governor of Qin province Moqi Pubo made rapid-as-lightning cavalry general, palace attendant of the third rank: in all editions "Qin" is written "Tai."
idiomatic: Moqi Pubo, commissioner with full powers, pacification-north general, commander-in-chief, and governor of Qin province, was made rapid-as-lightning cavalry general and palace attendant of the third rank; all editions write Qin as Tai.

literal: Comment: Moqi Pubo was governor of Qin province, repeatedly seen in Zhoushu juan 1, Annals of Emperor Wen, part 2, Yongxi year 3
idiomatic: Moqi Pubo was governor of Qin province, attested repeatedly in Zhoushu juan 1 (Annals of Emperor Wen, part 2), Yongxi year 3

literal: second month; same book, juan 2, Annals of Emperor Wen, part 2, Datong year 2
idiomatic: second month; Zhoushu juan 2 (same annals, part 2), Datong year 2

literal: fifth month; Beishi juan 6, Qi annals, part 1, Tianping year 3
idiomatic: fifth month; Beishi juan 6 (Qi annals, part 1), Tianping year 3

literal: second month; Beiqishu juan 27, Biography of Moqi Pubo, supplement.
idiomatic: second month; and Beiqishu juan 27 (Biography of Moqi Pubo, supplement).

literal: At the time there were two Qin provinces, one administered at Shanggui; this province from Yongan year 3
idiomatic: Two Qin provinces existed then. One, with its seat at Shanggui, from Yongan year 3

literal: after the rebel army was suppressed, Hou Mochen Yue, Zhao Gui, Li Bi, Nian Xian, and others successively were governors
idiomatic: after the rebel army was crushed, had Hou Mochen Yue, Zhao Gui, Li Bi, Nian Xian, and others as governors in turn

literal: (see Zhoushu juan 14 and juan 15, biographies of the various persons).
idiomatic: (see Zhoushu juan 14 and juan 15, their biographies).

literal: The other was Eastern Qin province, established at the end of Wei at Qian city.
idiomatic: The other was Eastern Qin, set up late in Wei at Qian city.

literal: This book, juan 9, Annals of Emperor Suzong, Xiaochang year 3, records Eastern Qin Governor Pan Yiyuan surrendered the rebel army with Qian city.
idiomatic: Juan 9 here (Annals of Emperor Suzong, Xiaochang year 3) records Eastern Qin governor Pan Yiyuan surrendering Qian city to the rebels.

literal: Taiping huanyu ji, juan 32, Long prefecture entry, lists successive changes.
idiomatic: Taiping huanyu ji, juan 32 (Long prefecture), traces the administrative shifts.

literal: Moqi Pubo must have been governor of Eastern Qin province.
idiomatic: Moqi Pubo must have governed Eastern Qin.

literal: Beishi juan 6, Qi basic annals, and Beiqishu juan 27, Biography of Moqi Pubo, both say after Gao Huan pacified Xia province, Moqi Pubo led his host to submit to Eastern Wei.
idiomatic: Beishi juan 6 (Qi basic annals) and Beiqishu juan 27 (Moqi Pubo) both say that after Gao Huan pacified Xia province, Moqi Pubo led his forces into Eastern Wei.

literal: This "Qin province" is near Xia province.
idiomatic: That Qin lay close to Xia province.

literal: Tai province is near Hedong; the circumstances do not fit.
idiomatic: Tai province stood near Hedong and does not suit the narrative.

literal: Here "Tai" is corruption of "Qin"; now corrected.
idiomatic: Tai here is a corruption of Qin; emended accordingly.

literal: Advanced enfeoffment to prince of a commandery: Beishi juan 5 writes "prince" as "duke."
idiomatic: His rank was advanced to prince of a commandery; Beishi juan 5 writes "prince" (wang) as "duke" (gong).

literal: Comment: Juan 101, Biography of Gaocang, also writes "duke."
idiomatic: Juan 101 (Biography of Gaocang) likewise has "duke."

literal: This was advancement from county marquis to commandery duke, not referring to the Gaocang royal title.
idiomatic: The promotion was from county marquis to commandery duke, not the kingship of Gaocang.

literal: Writing "duke" is correct.
idiomatic: "Duke" is the correct reading.

literal: Made rapid-as-lightning cavalry general, left guard general Yuan Binzhi Duke of Yingchuan: in all editions "chuan" is written "chang."
idiomatic: Yuan Binzhi, rapid-as-lightning cavalry general and left guard general, was made duke of Yingchuan; every edition writes "chuan" as "chang."

literal: Zhang Senkai states: "Beishi
idiomatic: Zhang Senkai notes: "Beishi

literal: (juan 5)
idiomatic: (juan 5)

literal: writes 'Yingchuan.'
idiomatic: has 'Yingchuan.'

literal: According to this book, Biography of Prince of Anle
idiomatic: This book's Biography of the Prince of Anle

literal: (juan 20, supplement)
idiomatic: (juan 20, supplement)

literal: Beiqishu, Annals of the Divine Warrior
idiomatic: Beiqishu (Annals of the Divine Warrior)

literal: (juan 2, supplement)
idiomatic: (juan 2, supplement)

literal: Zhoushu, Annals of Emperor Wen
idiomatic: and Zhoushu (Annals of Emperor Wen)

literal: (juan 2)
idiomatic: (juan 2)

literal: all write 'Yingchuan'; then the character 'chang' is error."
idiomatic: all read Yingchuan, so 'chang' is wrong."

literal: Comment: Northern Wei had no "Yingchang commandery"; the character "chang" is wrong; now emended according to Beishi.
idiomatic: Northern Wei had no Yingchang commandery; "chang" is erroneous and is emended from Beishi.

literal: Prince of Taiyuan Chang specially made rapid-as-lightning cavalry general. Comment: This book records promotions never with the wording "specially made"; the character "specially" likely was carried down from below "Yue Gong te" and is superfluous.
idiomatic: Wang Chang, prince of Taiyuan, was specially made rapid-as-lightning cavalry general. This book never uses "specially made" in promotion formulas; "specially" probably drifted down from the phrase "Yue Gong te" below and should be deleted.

literal: Day jiyou: Mao Hongbin of the Chun faction held Tong Pass; the Duke of Qi, Filial and Martial King, broke and captured him. Comment: Beishi juan 6, Qi basic annals, part 1, has Gao Huan take Tong Pass in the eighth month and return to Luoyang on gengyin in the ninth month; Zhoushu juan 1, Annals of Emperor Wen, part 1, and Beishi juan 9, Zhou basic annals, part 1, also say Gao Huan raided and took Tong Pass in the eighth month.
idiomatic: On jiyou, Mao Hongbin of Chun's faction held Tong Pass until the Duke of Qi, Filial and Martial King, stormed it and captured him. Beishi juan 6 (Qi basic annals, part 1) puts Gao Huan's capture of Tong Pass in the eighth month and his return to Luoyang on ninth-month gengyin; Zhoushu juan 1 (Annals of Emperor Wen, part 1) and Beishi juan 9 (Zhou basic annals, part 1) likewise date his seizure of the pass to the eighth month.

literal: Also according to Beishi, Wei annals, part 5, again says ninth month jiyou was the day Yuan Xiu counter-attacked Tong Pass and again took Hua province.
idiomatic: Beishi, Wei annals part 5, moreover makes ninth-month jiyou the day Yuan Xiu counterattacked Tong Pass and retook Hua province.

literal: Suspect here the recorded month and day all have errors.
idiomatic: The month and day given here are probably both wrong.

literal: Acting on Qing affairs Hou Yuan took Dongyang, beheaded Governor Prince of Donglai Gui Ping: in all editions "Dongyang" is written "Dongyang/Yang"
idiomatic: Hou Yuan, acting on Qing province affairs, took Dongyang and beheaded Governor Prince of Donglai Gui Ping; all editions miscopy Dongyang as Dong Yang or Dongyang province

literal: (one reading Yang)
idiomatic: (alternate reading Yang)

literal: province".
idiomatic: province."

literal: Comment: Juan 19, part 2, Biography of Prince of Anding Xiu, appendix Yuan Guiping biography, says at Emperor Chu's time "went out as governor of Qing province," and was harmed by Hou Yuan.
idiomatic: Juan 19, part 2 (Prince of Anding Xiu, appendix on Yuan Guiping) says that under Emperor Chu he "went out as governor of Qing province" and was killed by Hou Yuan.

literal: Juan 80, Biography of Hou Yuan, narrates this matter in great detail.
idiomatic: Juan 80 (Biography of Hou Yuan) tells the episode at length.

literal: Guiping was governor of Qing province; what Hou Yuan attacked was also Qing province.
idiomatic: Guiping governed Qing province, and Hou Yuan's target was Qing province.

literal: According to juan 106, Monograph on Geography, part 2, Qing province's seat was Dongyang.
idiomatic: Juan 106 (Monograph on Geography, part 2) places the seat of Qing province at Dongyang.

literal: Here the original text read "took Dongyang"; "yang" was corrupted to "Yang" or to the homophone "yang" meaning "to raise," later men groundlessly added the character "province"; now corrected.
idiomatic: The original line read "took Dongyang"; yang was miscopied as Yang or as the homophone for "to raise," and later copyists wrongly inserted "province"; all three errors are corrected here.
